routes.GET /api/integrations/files: Reusable WebDAV and SMB connections, including existing music sources with music_source:true. Listing reuses their saved identity and credentials without copying or moving the source.
routes.GET /api/integrations/files/edit?id=ID: Editable connection settings. Saved passwords and tokens are excluded.
routes.POST /api/integrations/files: Authorize a WebDAV or SMB connection using the corresponding /api/sources input. Saves the connection without selecting a music source or scanning music.
routes.PATCH /api/integrations/files: Edit a reusable connection with the files /api/sources update input. Editing a music source uses its existing configuration and keeps it in the library.
routes.GET /api/connect: Connect status: settings {enabled,name,profile,nearby,relay,public_relay,folder}, devices (continuable when the device recorded playback that continue {peer} can take, also while it is offline), invitation, connecting, emoji verification, joining progress as records received of the profile's total, and continuation, the newest playback of another paired device that this device can continue. Credentials and private keys are excluded. POST /api/connect with {action:enable,enabled:true} starts Connect. With enabled:false it stops all Connect activity and clears its configured state. Collection data and downloaded files remain. Enabling again creates a new profile. The existing HTTP controller port is unchanged.
routes.GET /api/connect/continuation: The device of the current continuation offer, or null. Paired devices sync their playback position, so a device that is offline now can still be offered. Does not contact devices or change playback.
routes.GET /api/connect/events: Follow Connect status changes as server-sent events.
routes.POST /api/connect: Use action enable {enabled}; join {invitation,replace:true} after confirming that joining removes this device's data; invite {peer}; pair {session,approve,replace:false}; cancel_pairing; rename {name}; remove {peer}; refresh; retry; discover; test_connection {peer}; network {nearby,relay,public_relay:false}; folder {folder:null|{path}|{document}|{connection,path}}; continue {peer}; control {peer,command:{command:play|pause|stop|next|previous|seek|volume,millis|value}}. Paired devices share source configs and saved logins, scrobbling accounts, shared preferences, favorites, ratings, listens, playlists, playlist folders, smart playlists, lyrics a person picks or edits, and analysis results. Lyrics fetched automatically that nobody picked are not shared. A change reaches online devices within seconds, and devices pass on what they received from others. Queues, downloads, download and stream quality, outputs and Local File Access mappings stay per device. Joining first clears this device's Rufin data, then receives the profile; original media files are not deleted. Another device's Local library appears as a source of kind peer: it browses offline, and plays and downloads while that device is online. folder sets a sync folder for devices that are never online together: a path on the running Rufin device, an Android document tree, or a path on a saved WebDAV or SMB connection (connection is its source ID). Files in the sync folder are encrypted with the profile key. Continue takes another device's queue and position and pauses that device when it is reachable. relay:null with public_relay:false disables relays; public_relay:true uses public Iroh relays; relay sets a custom relay URL.
routes.GET /api/playback: Playback status and the current track
routes.GET /api/pins: Read shared sidebar pins and their resolved items in saved order.
routes.POST /api/pins: Set a pin with {pin,pinned}. Pin is Album {source_id,album_id}, Artist {source_id,artist_id,album_artist}, Genre {source_id,genre_id}, Playlist {source_id,playlist_id}, SmartPlaylist {playlist_id} or PlaylistFolder {folder_id,smart}, wrapped in its type name. Library rows carry their pin as pin. IDs are object_id values, not numeric database keys; omit source_id for a local playlist.
routes.PATCH /api/pins: Reorder with {moved,target}, each a pin identity. Uses the desktop drag order: before when moving upward, after when moving downward.
routes.List order: Without sort or descending, a list or track page reads in the order saved for that list, the one the app opens it in. Responses name the order they read in as sort and descending. The sort choices are the orders the app offers for each list; position (a playlist list's order of creation, or a playlist's entry order) and definition (a smart playlist's saved order) are accepted API names the app does not offer.
routes.Pages: List responses carry page, the token of the page they read: {route, source, folder, options}. GET /api/page?page=TOKEN reads it again with offset, limit (up to 128), total, q, sort and descending; an opened smart playlist's token keeps the time it opened at. POST /api/queue with {page, mode} plays the page whole in its order and filter; with index it plays the page from that row. With ranges, a list of {start, end} row ranges, POST /api/queue plays or queues those rows, POST /api/playlists and /api/playlists/entries add them, DELETE /api/playlists/entries removes them, POST /api/favorite sets their tracks' favorite, and GET /api/favorite?page=...&ranges=... reads whether all of them are favorites. Card rows (albums, artists, genres, playlists, smart playlists, playlist folders) carry the token of the page they open as page in HTML responses.
routes.Row fields: Library rows (albums, artists, playlists, smart_playlists, Home items, tracks and entries) carry kind (track, album, artist, genre, mood, playlist, smart-playlist or playlist-folder) and fields [{field,text}]: what the app shows for the row in its list, the labels under a card's title or a track list's columns, in the list's saved order. Track pages also carry columns, that list's fields. field is a name such as RowIndex, Image, Title, TitleMerged (title with artist), Artist, AlbumArtist, Album, Year, SongCount, Duration, Favorite or Tools (the row's actions).
routes.Queue drop position: POST /api/queue and its collection routes accept mode insert with before or after (zero-based queue position). Omit both to insert at the end. Uses the desktop drop operation without starting playback. POST /api/queue/reorder also accepts before or after.
routes.GET /api/sources: Your sources and the source currently in use
Saved source settings, without passwords or tokens.

POST /api/sources/library.library: library ID, or null for All Music

Home sections in the app's order with the app's titles: the visible blocks in their configured order, with the server's own sections right after the Showcase. Each section lists its tracks, then its albums. You can set folder, or block to read one block's section.
routes.POST /api/sources: Connect, save and select a source, then scan its music in the background. Returns the source ID after selection. Follow /api/sources/events for scan progress. See source_setup for examples.
routes.PATCH /api/sources: Change source settings. See source_update for examples.
routes.POST /api/downloads: Download tracks with {uris:[track URI]}. Each track goes to its source's download location in that source's download quality, as a download started in the app does. Returns without waiting for the downloads.
routes.GET /api/downloads/cache-settings: Read artwork and lyrics caching choices across all sources and whether artists and albums sort by their sort tags, as {artwork:bool,lyrics:bool,sort_tags:bool}. True downloads automatically; false downloads lazily.
routes.POST /api/downloads/cache-settings: Set caching choices across all sources and the sort tag choice with {artwork:bool,lyrics:bool,sort_tags:bool}. Automatic downloads include existing and newly scanned entries. Returns the saved choices.
routes.POST /api/downloads/quality: Set a source download profile with {source:source ID,quality:original|{transcoded:{codec:opus|aac|mp3|vorbis|flac,bitrate_kbps:128,channels:preserve|stereo_lossy|stereo}}}. Bitrate presets run from 64 through 320 kbps in 16 kbps steps. FLAC ignores bitrate. Rufin uses server transcoding when suitable and otherwise encodes the original locally. The quality applies to downloads that have not started; tracks already downloaded keep their copy. To change one part as the app's control does, send the shown quality with edit {codec:null|codec} (null is the original), {bitrate_kbps:160} or {channels:...}; the app picks the bitrate a new codec starts at. Returns the saved quality and download_quality {value,bitrate,channels}: whether it offers a bitrate and channels.
routes.POST /api/downloads/clear-artwork-cache: Clear the artwork cache across sources. Keeps artwork for completed and active music downloads, authored playlist artwork and source files. Takes no body and returns after clearing.
routes.POST /api/downloads/clear-lyrics-cache: Clear cached lyrics across sources. Keeps lyrics for completed and active music downloads, edited lyrics and source files. Takes no body and returns after clearing.
routes.GET /api/sources/progress: Check progress while adding, switching, refreshing or downloading source artwork and lyrics.
routes.GET /api/sources/events: Follow source progress, starting with the current status.
routes.POST /api/sources/login/nextcloud: Sign in through your browser. Send {settings: file_settings, credentials: {secret,headers}}. Returns a login link, then the login details to use when adding the source.
routes.GET /api/sources/plex/logins: Saved Plex accounts. Reuse one to add another server or profile.
routes.POST /api/sources/plex/profiles: List Plex profiles. Send {login} from a completed login. Returns {login,profiles}.
routes.POST /api/sources/plex/servers: List Plex servers. Send {login,profile,pin:null,lan:[]}. Returns {login,servers} to use when adding the source.
routes.POST /api/sources/smb/shares: List network shares. Send {settings: file_settings, credentials: {secret,headers}}.
routes.GET /api/tracks?source=...&offset=0&limi: Browse tracks from a source, up to 256 at a time. You can also set folder, sort, descending and favorites.
routes.GET /api/albums?source=...&offset=0&limi: Browse albums, up to 128 at a time. You can also set folder, q, sort, descending and favorites.
routes.GET /api/albums/tracks?id=...&offset=0&l: Browse tracks in an album, up to 128 at a time. You can also set q, sort, descending and favorites. The album lists whole (see music_folders). The response includes album_tracks and disc_sections: pairs of zero-based track position and disc number in the filtered result. Sections are empty for a single known disc or a sort other than track_number; disc number 0 means unknown.
Browse folders saved in Rufin, up to 128 at a time. Set parent to open a folder, or folder to choose where browsing starts. Use the folder IDs returned by this API.
Browse source folders. File sources use their saved directory inventory; other sources browse the server directly. You can set parent and folder. Returned track_ids match object_id in track results.
routes.GET /api/playlists?offset=0&limit=100: Browse playlists that are not tied to a source, with playlist folders as rows of kind playlist-folder; a folder's playlists list under it with playlist_folder=ID. Set source to include its playlists too. Up to 128 at a time; you can also set q, sort and descending.
The playlists tracks can be added to, Rufin's own and the source's, whose names hold q (any case), in the playlist list's order: limit of them from offset (default 100 from 0) and how many there are, as {count,playlists:[{id,name}]}.
routes.Playlist ownership: POST /api/playlists accepts source (owner, null for Rufin), uris or a selection to start with (see playlist_selection; its source is selection_source, as source names the owner), and public (optional visibility for supported server playlists). Omit public to keep the existing creation default. Newly created playlists are pinned like in the desktop app.
routes.Playlist updates: name and public are optional; omitted fields are unchanged. public applies to supported server playlists.
Delete a playlist through its owner. Rufin-owned linked playlists are removed from Rufin and their files remain on disk.
Read playlist visibility. public is a boolean, or null when unavailable.
Read the linked file, path display, saved error, refresh, save, and path options.
routes.GET /api/playlists/source-settings?sourc: Read the source default for automatic playlist saving.
routes.PATCH /api/playlists/source-settings: Set {source,auto_save}; linked playlists without an override inherit this setting.
routes.POST /api/playlists/import: Import {paths,source,copy}. paths is an array of M3U/M3U8/PLS/XSPF paths on the Rufin host or relative to source. copy defaults to false, retaining the file link.
routes.POST /api/playlists/export: Export {id,path,source,path_mode,linked}. The filename selects M3U/M3U8/PLS/XSPF. source is optional; without it path is on the Rufin host. linked defaults to false.
routes.PATCH /api/playlists/file: Edit with {id,name,auto_refresh,auto_save,path_mode}. auto_save is null to inherit the source default, false, or true. path_mode is automatic, relative, or absolute.
routes.POST /api/playlists/file: Run {id,action,force,path,source}. Actions are save, reload, unlink, delete, link, or rename. rename takes a sibling filename in path. link loads the file unless force is true, which writes the playlist. source is optional; without it path is on the Rufin host. force explicitly overwrites external file changes for save or discards unsaved playlist edits for reload.
Browse tracks in a playlist, up to 256 at a time. You can set offset, limit, q, sort and descending. Sort accepts track_sort choices or position for playlist order. The playlist lists whole (see music_folders).
routes.POST /api/playlists/remove-unavailable?i: Remove confirmed missing tracks from a Rufin global or file playlist. A failed availability check leaves the playlist unchanged. Returns {removed}. Does not delete media files.
routes.GET /api/queue: Tracks around the current queue position and the total count. Set limit to choose how many nearby tracks to return (up to 100).
routes.POST /api/queue/clear: Clear the queue, including from a browser form.
routes.DELETE /api/queue: Clear the queue using the app's setting for keeping the current song.
Get a track's album, artists and favorite state. Album URIs return their artists. page, a page token, names the source and music folder the links open in; without it they open in the selected ones.
routes.POST /api/favorite: Set favorite with {kind: track, album or artist, uri, favorite: true or false}. Returns the effective favorite state.
routes.POST /api/queue/radio: Play radio with {kind: track, uri} or {kind: album, artist, album_artist, genre or playlist, id}. Library rows offer theirs in menu.radio in HTML responses.
routes.POST /api/queue/item: Remove a queue row with {position}, including from a browser form.
Remove a track from the queue
routes.GET /api/lyrics: Lyrics for the current track, with line and word timings when available.
routes.POST /api/lyrics: Load lyrics for the current track using your lyrics settings.
routes.GET /api/lyrics/events: Follow lyrics updates. The media_uri and run match the current playback media.
Track or album cover as PNG. Set size to the displayed physical pixel size. Add original=true for the original format, including animation. Returns 404 if unavailable.

POST /api/queue/reorder.before: zero-based queue position, or null for the end

routes.GET /api/events: Follow playback, source progress, catalog changes and lyrics together on one connection. The first update names the stream as stream. Pass page=TOKEN to follow that page; a library read sent with the header X-Rufin-Events: STREAM becomes the page the stream follows. A catalog change then carries page_refresh (reread: read the page again where it is; reopen: open it again) when it changes what the page shows, and states [{uri,favorite,rating}] for tracks, albums and artists whose favorite or rating changed, which rows that show them can patch in.
Browse artists. Use offset, limit (up to 128), q, sort, descending, favorites and album_artists.
Browse an artist’s tracks, up to 256 at a time. Use q, sort, descending and album_artists.
Browse tracks in a genre. Use q, sort, descending, offset and limit, and source and folder as music_folders describes.
Browse saved smart playlists and their folders (rows of kind playlist-folder; open one with playlist_folder=ID), up to 64 at a time. Source is optional; use q, sort and descending.
Browse tracks selected by the saved playlist rules and limit. Use source, q, offset, limit (up to 256), sort and descending. Sort accepts track_sort choices or definition for the saved playlist order. An opened smart playlist keeps the members it opened with: pass opened (Unix seconds of the first read) on every later read of the page, so plays, ratings and syncs change its members only when it is opened again.
routes.POST /api/playback/auto-dj: Toggle Auto DJ using the app’s existing settings.
Saved random-play settings and genres. Use q and offset to browse genres, 64 at a time.
routes.GET /api/equalizer: Current equalizer editor. Optional output selects an existing output identity; omitted follows the selected output.
routes.POST /api/equalizer: Shared EQ operations: preview {output,edit}, commit {output}, select {output,preset:null or ID}, save {output,name:null or text}, duplicate {output,name}, rename {id,name}, delete {id}, import {output,text,format:Json|Apo}, export {output,format}, assign {output,assigned}, apply {output}. Edits use enum objects such as {BandGain:{index:0,value:6}} and {Enabled:{value:true}}. Preview does not write settings; commit persists the final editor. Cast previews await apply except discrete bypass/format changes.
routes.GET /api/equalizer/presets: Built-in and named custom preset identities and names. Custom is the retained draft, selected with preset:null.
routes.GET /api/equalizer/events: Equalizer server-sent events. Optional output, meter=true and spectrum=true. Measurement stops when the connection closes.
routes.GET /api/equalizer/response: Calculated response from the shared filter model, with frequency and dB arrays. Uses actual stream sample rate or 48 kHz for preview.

commands: Playback and queue commands return 202 when received. Check playback status or follow playback updates to see the result or any error. Source and playlist changes return when finished. Use IDs exactly as returned, including negative numbers. Positions and offsets start at zero. Each copy of a track in a playlist or queue has its own ID.
login: Keep the login connection open until sign-in finishes. Closing it cancels sign-in. Updates use event: login with JSON {event,data}, or {error}. Plex also accepts {method: password, data: {username,password,verification_code:null}}; Emby accepts {method: password, data: {username,password}}. Use the returned login details unchanged when adding the source.

source_setup.web_dav_smb: {type: web_dav or smb, data: {name, settings: file_settings below, credentials: {secret,headers:[]}}}
source_setup.emby_connect: {type: emby_connect, data: {server: a server from the login result,source_name:null,use_instant_mix:false}}

source_update.files: {type: files, data: {source_id,name,settings: file_settings,credentials:{secret:null,headers:null}}}. Use null to keep the saved password and headers.
source_update.other_types: For open_subsonic, emby_connect and jellyfin_quick_connect, add source_id to the corresponding source_setup data.

folder_exclusions: Local, WebDAV and SMB sources accept excluded_folders in their source settings. These paths skip folder discovery, including subfolders. Local paths may be absolute or relative to each music root. WebDAV and SMB paths are relative to the source URL, with forward slashes. Paths need not exist or belong to the current library. Included CUE files and playlists can still reference audio in excluded folders. An empty list clears exclusions. Omitting excluded_folders from a Local update preserves the saved list.
browsing: Use offset to skip results, limit to choose how many to return, q to search, sort to choose the order, descending to reverse it, and favorites to show only favorites. A track page without sort or descending lists in the order its list is set to, as the other clients show it, and its response names that sort and descending. Track, album, artist, playlist and smart-playlist pages accept total=true to include the matching result count; otherwise total is null. Reuse that count while browsing the same results instead of requesting it for every window. The random genre picker also accepts total=true. Browsing or refreshing a source does not switch the source currently in use.
events: Update routes use server-sent events (SSE). Each data line contains JSON. The combined events route also follows theme changes.
browser: GET / serves full HTML pages for login, browsing and playback without JavaScript. POST /session accepts a token form field and sets a persistent HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. Reconnecting renews the same browser session so open tabs remain valid. It survives browser and controller restarts while the API token is unchanged. Signing out clears the browser cookie; changing the API token invalidates existing cookies. Accept: application/json returns the browser CSRF token. Cookie-authenticated API writes require X-Rufin-CSRF for JSON requests or a csrf form field. The same API routes accept browser forms and redirect after success; logout forms also require csrf. API clients can continue using Authorization: Bearer without cookies.
html: Library browsing routes return HTML for the web page when HX-Request is true. Other callers receive JSON.
playlist_selection: When creating a playlist or adding entries, selection can replace uris: {kind: album, artist, genre, playlist or smart_playlist, id}; an artist also takes album_artists. The tracks are what the collection's page lists, in its saved order, in the source and music folder the request names (see music_folders): source and folder on POST /api/playlists/entries, selection_source and folder on POST /api/playlists.
music_folders: folder is a music folder id from GET /api/sources (libraries), read with source. It narrows that source's tracks in the lists (tracks, albums, artists, genres, moods, favorites, folders), Home, search, artist, genre and mood pages, smart playlists and random play. Albums and playlists stay whole, and the playlist lists follow source only. Collections of other sources are never narrowed. Without a folder, reads cover every folder.

queue_modes.replace: Play now and replace the queue
queue_modes.append: Add to the end of the queue

collection_playback: For queue/source, queue/album, queue/artist and queue/playlist, q, sort and descending choose the tracks and order. Set anchor_uri to start at a particular track. For a playlist with repeated tracks, use anchor_entry to choose the playlist entry. Without an anchor, Play follows your shuffle setting. Without sort or descending, a collection plays in the order its page lists in, as the app plays it; sort definition plays a smart playlist in its saved order.
volume: Volume is a slider position from 0 to 1. Rufin applies the perceptual or linear scale selected in the app. Set persist to false while dragging, then send the final value with persist true to save it.
